slices.focus: Tasha adds monthly therapy for boundaries and grief load after noticing emotional spillover
slices.summary: A winter string of deaths and evening calls leaves Tasha replaying family conversations at home — still in her coat, thinking about someone else's loved one instead of her own evening. Renee pushes her to stop treating informal coping as sufficient and to protect a regular therapy appointment focused on clinical boundaries and grief load, not just professional talk. The agent helps her plan a short post-call reset (write one sentence, wash dishes/shower, soft gospel music), bring the clustered-loss pattern (not just individual cases) into therapy, and measure the appointment by 'relief and honesty, not polish.' Tasha plans to keep the monthly appointment protected, build the after-hours sequence, and avoid normalizing carrying people home just because she is still functioning.
